source.title: Typical and atypical solutions in non-convex neural networks with discrete and continuous weights
source.authors: Carlo Baldassi; E. M. Malatesta; Gabriele Perugini; R. Zecchina

record.tranche_reason: Measures teacher-student generalization in negative-margin perceptrons, a setting outside the listed claim versions. It does not test random-label memorization or the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, model-size, sharpness, or example-removal claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports generalization error for students trained at different margins in a teacher-student setting. Its cited discussion of other work is not recorded as results. Figures 7 and 13 give curves without tabulated values.
record.test_reason: The study measures teacher-student generalization in negative-margin perceptrons, which fits none of V1–V8. Its flatness measure is local entropy, not magnitude-aware sharpness; it neither measures generalization gaps nor ranks sharpness against norm- and margin-based measures. The discussion of Jiang et al. is a citation, not a replication of V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the generalization findings: wide, flat solutions can generalize well even at strongly negative training margins, with algorithm-dependent robustness. The paper's broader conclusions concern solution geometry and a local-entropy transition, which strongly affects algorithmic accessibility in binary models but apparently does not impose the same barrier in spherical models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses perceptrons with random Gaussian patterns and teacher-generated labels, and studies negative-margin learning and solution geometry rather than natural-label generalization alongside random-label memorization.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization varies with student margin and, for the spherical case, algorithm details such as the cross-entropy effective temperature or simulated-annealing cooling schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections VI.B and E.4 report good teacher-student generalization at strongly negative training margins when algorithms reach wide, flat regions; performance depends on algorithm bias and settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In spherical and binary teacher-student perceptrons, algorithms biased toward wide, flat solutions can retain good generalization despite weak negative-margin training constraints.

record.problems: The generalization results are presented as figures without tabulated values. The numerical teacher-student results average over a limited number of teacher realizations and restarts; the text gives no error bars for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No reported generalization result rows were left out. Local-entropy, training-error, and solution-geometry results do not measure generalization and were not included.

untested.parts: No matched comparison of random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep measuring test error beyond interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison under specified tuning budgets.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware perturbation measure, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized examples and matched random-removal control.

record.verdict_notes: A new setting warrants T3 only when its results bear on a listed version. Generalization and flatness terminology alone does not link these perceptron results to V7.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting random labels with fitting natural labels using the same architecture and recipe.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with the generalization gap.

rows.subject: spherical negative perceptron
rows.size_stated: N = 2000 in Fig. 6; not stated for Fig. 7
rows.operation_detail: Trained student perceptrons at fixed negative margin in a teacher-student setting; generalization error evaluated at zero margin.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over 10 independent teacher realizations and 10 random restarts for each dataset.
rows.note: The text says good generalization is found when learning converges into wide flat minima, including at very negative margins; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The generalization result fits no version, so partial is inappropriate. N = 2000 belongs to the separate Fig. 6 experiment and should be removed from this row; Fig. 7 does not specify N.
